title: Quantum Brownian motion in a temperature gradient
authors: Ricardo J. S. Afonso, Pedro V. Paraguassú, Thiago Werlang, Daniel Valente
abstract: When a classical Brownian particle is subjected to a temperature gradient it can undergo thermophoresis, i.e., the particle gets transported towards the colder regions of the environment, which bears relevant consequences to nonequilibrium self-organization. Here, we investigate how the quantum Brownian motion is affected by a temperature gradient. We employ a recently proposed generalized system-plus-reservoir model, where one assumes a continuum field of thermal baths. As our main result, we obtain the quantum influence functional, within the Feynmann-Vernon path integral approach. To test convergence, we derive an effective Langevin equation for the center of mass of the quantum wavepacket, and show that it coincides with the classical Langevin equation at high temperatures. Both the fully quantum (low temperatures) and the semiclassical (high temperature) limits show signatures of quantum thermophoresis in the quantum Brownian motion, a so far unexplored effect.
summary: This paper theoretically investigates quantum Brownian motion subjected to a temperature gradient, leading to the prediction of quantum thermophoresis. Using the Feynman-Vernon path integral approach, the authors derive the exact quantum influence functional and an effective Langevin equation. The results confirm that quantum effects manifest in both the low and high-temperature limits, extending classical understanding into the quantum domain.
main_problem: The paper investigates how quantum Brownian motion is affected by a spatially varying temperature gradient, focusing on the phenomenon of quantum thermophoresis.
main_result: The authors derive an exact quantum influence functional and show that both the fully quantum (low T) and semiclassical (high T) limits exhibit signatures of quantum thermophoresis.
method: The primary method involves using the Feynman-Vernon path integral approach to derive the influence functional, followed by deriving an effective, non-Markovian quantum Langevin equation.
model_or_system: The system is a quantum Brownian particle coupled to a bath modeled as a continuum of local thermal baths, allowing for a position-dependent temperature profile T(X).
key_observables: The quantum influence functional F[x, x'], the effective Langevin equation for the center of mass, and the derived friction coefficient $\eta_{	ext{eff}}[x]$ and diffusion coefficient $D_{	ext{eff}}(x)$.
important_parameters: Temperature gradient T(X), high-temperature limit, low-temperature limit, and the Ohmic regime.
main_assumptions: The environment is modeled as a continuum of independent local baths, and the derivation relies on path integral techniques and approximations in the semiclassical limit.
paper_structure: The paper builds from the generalized system-plus-reservoir model to derive the influence functional via path integrals. It then analyzes the resulting dynamics by deriving the effective Langevin equation, examining the high-temperature and low-temperature limits to confirm quantum thermophoresis.
why_interesting: This work provides a rigorous quantum generalization of classical thermophoresis, extending the analysis into the quantum regime where non-equilibrium effects are crucial for understanding self-organization.
